description: What operators, brands and MVNOs state on their own pages about their services (rule round 32, part A). Each statement names its source page, the day it was read and a paraphrase, never quoted text. A statement says what the operator sells, not what a tariff includes or a phone supports. Only sets_value statements change a value: an MMS end that the operator states network-wide, checked by a second reader, which makes the profiles of its networks publish mms unsupported and enabledMMS false from operator_statement.
display_rule: Show an offered status as: the operator states it offers the service (read on <checked_at>); whether your tariff includes it is not checked. Show an end as: the operator states the service ended on <last_day>. Never show a statement as works. A host-only brand shows only as a brand on its host network, never as a statement about the SIM.

statements.paraphrase: Salt states that it discontinues its MMS service from 10 January 2023, as the other main Swiss operators do.
Sunrise states that it discontinues its MMS service as of 17 March 2024; TalkTalk and Lebara, which run on Sunrise, state the same for their customers.

sources.publisher: TalkTalk Switzerland, an MVNO on Sunrise
Lebara Switzerland, an MVNO on Sunrise

statements.paraphrase: The 1&1 mobile service description treats the physical SIM card and the eSIM profile together as the SIM, so 1&1 provides eSIM profiles; it also mentions Multi-Cards in eSIM format for an Apple Watch.
1&1 states that its MMS service ended on 30 June 2026 and has not been available since 1 July 2026, and that MMS is switched off in every German network.
ALDI TALK states that it offers an eSIM; existing customers swap via the service hotline, new customers first get a starter set; the swap is free and the eSIM works only in phones for now.

ALDI TALK states that its 4G/LTE network offers telephony in HD quality and that the phone should support VoLTE, sometimes switched on in settings, to call over LTE. The page dates from the 3G switch-off period.
ALDI TALK states that WLAN-Telefonie lets customers call over WLAN instead of the mobile network, at home and abroad, billed per tariff; a compatible phone and the setting switched on are needed.
ALDI TALK states that WLAN-Telefonie works in Germany and abroad, with calls billed according to the tariff.
congstar states that the eSIM can be booked free of charge with all Allnet Flat tariffs and prepaid tariffs; it is chosen as the SIM format in the cart.
congstar states that MMS is part of its contracts only until 30 June 2026 and no longer available afterwards, and names RCS as the alternative.

sources.publisher: congstar price list, a brand of Telekom Deutschland

statements.paraphrase: congstar states that all its tariffs have been enabled for VoLTE since September 2020; a VoLTE-capable phone is needed.

sources.publisher: congstar (help page on VoIP, VoLTE and WLAN-Call)

statements.paraphrase: congstar states that mobile calls currently run only over 4G with VoLTE and that 5G is used for data only; voice over 5G is described as a future step. The page shows no date.

sources.publisher: congstar (help page on VoIP, VoLTE and WLAN-Call)

statements.paraphrase: congstar states that WLAN-Call lets customers call where mobile reception is poor, with no extra cost or effort; a WLAN-Call capable phone and the setting switched on are needed.

sources.publisher: congstar (help page on VoIP, VoLTE and WLAN-Call)

statements.paraphrase: congstar states that WLAN-Call works over any private or public WLAN and is therefore available worldwide; abroad, outgoing WLAN calls are billed like calls from Germany.

sources.publisher: congstar (help page on VoIP, VoLTE and WLAN-Call)

statements.paraphrase: fraenk states that customers choose between an eSIM and a classic SIM card when ordering; the eSIM is free.
fraenk answers in its FAQ that Voice over LTE can be used with its tariff.
fraenk answers in its FAQ that WLAN-Call (WiFi calling) can be used with its tariff.

fraenk states that outside the EU, with a stable WLAN, calls and SMS to Germany work over WLAN-Call in both directions; it has tested this in some countries, not all. Inside the EU it advises switching WLAN-Call off.

LIDL Connect states in its tariff notes that WLAN calls are possible where mobile coverage is limited, once activated in the app or web portal and on a phone that supports them; tariff terms apply, no extra cost.

sources.publisher: LIDL Connect (customer account FAQ and tariff notes)

statements.paraphrase: Telefónica states that o2 has offered nationwide access to its 5G standalone network, sold as 5G Plus, since autumn 2023; customers need the 5G Plus pack, free for twelve months, so pack-dependent.
o2 describes ordering and activating an eSIM for new contracts, existing customers, Apple Watch and prepaid; swapping a SIM card to an eSIM is free.
o2 states that its MMS service is no longer available from 30 June 2026 and names RCS as the successor. The listed MMSC hosts are Telefonica's current MMSC and the former E-Plus MMSC on 26203.

sources.publisher: o2 community, announcement by an o2 moderator

statements.paraphrase: Telefónica states on its o2 Business pages that VoLTE with HD voice is available free to o2 business customers with a VoLTE-capable phone; the statement found is on the business site.
Telefónica states that with 5G Plus its customers have Voice over New Radio for calls over 5G; a later note says iPhone users can now browse and call over the o2 5G standalone network.
o2 states that WLAN-Telefonie is in principle available to all o2 customers with an LTE, 4G or 5G capable tariff, a capable phone and the setting switched on.
o2 states that its WLAN-Telefonie works both in Germany and abroad; calls over WLAN abroad are billed as if made in Germany.
Telekom states that its free 5G+ Ultra add-on for private customers runs on its existing 5G standalone network; access to 5G SA is through this option, so tariff-dependent.
Telekom states that its customers can move their eSIM profile between Android and iOS devices, in addition to same-system transfers offered since earlier years.

sources.publisher: Deutsche Telekom (media information on eSIM transfer)

statements.paraphrase: Telekom states that calls over 4G/LTE (VoLTE) are possible in all its tariffs at no extra cost; after the 3G switch-off calls run over 2G or VoLTE. The statement dates from the 2020 switch-off announcement.

sources.publisher: Deutsche Telekom (media information on the 3G switch-off)

statements.paraphrase: Telekom explains that WLAN Call works abroad and calls and texts over it are billed as if the customer were in Germany; it can save money outside the EU and may cost extra for local calls inside the EU.
Vodafone announced that 5G+ (5G standalone) is switched on nationwide for private customers; access is unlocked free of charge, for example in the MeinVodafone app.
Vodafone states that new customers can order an eSIM with a contract or with a CallYa prepaid card, and existing customers can swap to an eSIM in MeinVodafone.
Vodafone states that it switched off its MMS service in the Vodafone network on 17 January 2023, after 21 years; SMS stays.
Vodafone states that VoLTE is switched on by default in its mobile contracts at no extra cost; if it is missing, support can enable it.

Vodafone marks the roaming partner networks where calls over 4G/LTE (VoLTE roaming) work and explains that a VoLTE-roaming capable phone with a recent iOS or Android version is needed; country- and partner-dependent.
Vodafone states that at many sites voice calls over 5G (VoNR) are already possible on its 5G+ network, while calls are otherwise carried over 2G and 4G; site-dependent.
Vodafone states that WiFi Calling is included automatically and free in almost all its tariffs and lists the postpaid and CallYa tariffs that have it; tariff-dependent.
Vodafone states that WiFi Calling does not work abroad; there the phone uses the mobile network for calls.
POST states that sending and receiving MMS ended on 29 September 2024, also to and from other networks. Join, an MVNO on 27001 with its own MMSC, is not covered.
Maxis states, on its Hotlink FAQ, that it discontinues MMS completely, effective 15 March 2026, as part of network modernisation.
